another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to understand your situation. 

**Do you have a child you're claiming for?** If yes, please tell me:
- Their name (or what you'd like to call them)
- Their age

This will help me determine which eligibility path applies to you. Child Benefit eligibility depends on the child's age and circumstances:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children 20 or over are not eligible

How old is your child?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I'm enquiring about my daughter Alex. She's 8 years old and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have Alex, your 8-year-old daughter who lives with you at home.

Since Alex is under 16, let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - at 8 years old, Alex is under 16. Now I need to check a few more things:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

I expect at 8 years old she's not working, but I need to confirm this to continue the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not working at all - she's only 8, so she's just in primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect, that makes sense! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in her own right?** 

For example, is she receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in her own name? 

Again, at 8 years old this would be very unusual, but I need to confirm she's not receiving these types of benefits in her own right to proceed.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she doesn't receive any benefits in her own name - she's just a child.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent, let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

At 8 years old and in primary school, I assume she's not, but I need to confirm she's not in a disqualifying apprenticeship program to continue.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, of course not - she's only 8 and in primary school, so no apprenticeship.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me move forward with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to check your residency status. 

**Do you meet the UK residency requirements?**

You can qualify if ANY of the following apply to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold)
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (for up to 91 days)
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself and family
6. You have pre-settled status as a student with sufficient resources
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

**Which of these applies to you?** The most common is simply that you normally live in the UK.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK - we live in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You meet the residency requirement by normally living in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

You meet this requirement if ANY of the following apply:

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already mentioned you do)
2. You contribute to Alex's upkeep by paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit towards their care (food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents)
3. You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement

Since you've already told me Alex lives with you at home, you clearly meet the first requirement. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member
- Anyone else

Please let me know:
- If no one else is claiming, or
- If someone else is claiming but you've both agreed you should claim instead, or
- If there's a dispute about who should claim

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, no one else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand Alex's living situation. You mentioned she lives with you at home, but I need to check if any special circumstances apply:

**Which of the following describes Alex's current living situation?**

- She's currently in hospital
- She's in local authority care
- She's fostered
- **She's living normally at home with you** (this seems to be your situation based on what you've told me)

Can you confirm she's just living normally at home with you, with none of these special circumstances?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - she's just living normally at home with me. No hospital, care, or fostering - just a regular home situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council paying anything towards Alex's living costs or care? 

Generally, you cannot get Child Benefit if the local council is paying for the child's accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm covering all her costs myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent news! Let me get the final outcome for you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You ARE Eligible for Child Benefit!

**Result: ELIGIBLE**

You meet all the Child Benefit eligibility requirements for Alex. Based on our assessment:

✅ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)  
✅ She's not working  
✅ She doesn't receive benefits in her own right  
✅ She's not in an apprenticeship  
✅ You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for her  
✅ No one else is claiming for Alex  
✅ Alex lives at home normally with you  
✅ The council isn't paying towards her care  

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may need to pay back some or all of the Child Benefit through your tax return
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

### How to Apply:
Visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Congratulations! You should be able to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

All eligibility criteria are satisfied.
